dedupe_keys.name: strong ground motion data of the 2015 gorkha nepal earthquake sequence in the kathmandu valley

description: Strong ground motion data of the 2015 Gorkha Nepal earthquake sequence in the Kathmandu Valley is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Michiko Shigefuji et al. Strong-motion records of earthquakes are used to evaluate the source rupture process, seismic wave propagation and strong ground motion characteristics, and to provide valuable data for earthquake disaster mitigation. The Kathmandu Valley, Nepal, which is characterised by having soft sediments that have been deposited in an earthquake-prone zone, has experienced numerous earthquakes. Coverage: national (NP); published in 2022. Formats: TXT. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 31869369 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
